blocks.en: "But of that day and hour no one knows... but only the Father." — Matthew 24:36 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Pero del día y la hora nadie sabe... sino sólo mi Padre." — Mateo 24:36 (RVG)

blocks.en: Introduction: The End as Purpose, Not Panic
blocks.es_reference: Introducción: El Fin como Propósito, No Pánico

blocks.en: The doctrine of last things—eschatology—addresses the culmination of God's redemptive plan. It speaks of the return of Christ, the final judgment, the resurrection of the dead, and the eternal state of both the righteous and the unrighteous. But from the beginning, we must understand something clearly. Eschatology is often treated as a subject of speculation. People want charts, timelines, and predictions. They want to know when.
blocks.es_reference: La doctrina de las últimas cosas—la escatología—aborda la culminación del plan redentor de Dios. Habla del regreso de Cristo, el juicio final, la resurrección de los muertos y el estado eterno tanto de los justos como de los injustos. Pero desde el principio, debemos entender algo claramente. La escatología a menudo se trata como un tema de especulación. La gente quiere gráficos, cronologías y predicciones. Quieren saber cuándo.

blocks.en: Scripture consistently redirects that desire. The focus is not prediction. The focus is preparation. Jesus did not teach His followers how to calculate the end. He taught them how to be ready when it comes. History is not random. It is moving toward a conclusion established by God. Christ has come. Christ will come again. The question is not: Can you explain the end? The question is: Are you prepared for it?
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura redirige consistentemente ese deseo. El enfoque no es la predicción. El enfoque es la preparación. Jesús no enseñó a Sus seguidores cómo calcular el fin. Les enseñó cómo estar listos cuando llegue. La historia no es aleatoria. Se mueve hacia una conclusión establecida por Dios. Cristo ha venido. Cristo vendrá otra vez. La pregunta no es: ¿Puedes explicar el fin? La pregunta es: ¿Estás preparado para él?

blocks.en: "It is appointed for men to die once, but after this the judgment." — Hebrews 9:27
blocks.es_reference: "Está establecido para los hombres que mueran una sola vez, y después de esto el juicio." — Hebreos 9:27

blocks.en: Jesus' Teaching on the End: Readiness Above Revelation
blocks.es_reference: La Enseñanza de Jesús sobre el Fin: Preparación Sobre Revelación

blocks.en: The disciples asked three questions recorded in Matthew 24: (1) When will the Temple be destroyed? (2) When will You return? (3) What will be the sign of the end of the age? Jesus answered them together, weaving near and far prophecies into a single discourse. The Temple was destroyed in AD 70, a catastrophic event that fulfilled His words. The return of Christ and the end of the age remain future. Because the questions are answered together, it is not always immediately clear which event is being described in any given verse. This is not confusion. It is intentional. Jesus is not giving a timeline. He is shaping a life.
blocks.es_reference: Los discípulos hicieron tres preguntas registradas en Mateo 24: (1) ¿Cuándo será destruido el Templo? (2) ¿Cuándo regresarás? (3) ¿Cuál será la señal del fin del siglo? Jesús les respondió juntas, entretejiendo profecías cercanas y lejanas en un solo discurso. El Templo fue destruido en el año 70 d.C., un evento catastrófico que cumplió Sus palabras. El regreso de Cristo y el fin del siglo siguen siendo futuros. Debido a que las preguntas son respondidas juntas, no siempre es inmediatamente claro qué evento se describe en cualquier versículo dado. Esto no es confusión. Es intencional. Jesús no está dando una cronología. Está moldeando una vida.

blocks.en: His emphasis is clear: watch, be ready, stay faithful. The parables reinforce this message: ten virgins—five prepared, five foolish; servants entrusted with talents—faithful or unfaithful; people going about daily life—suddenly separated. The issue is not when. The issue is readiness.
blocks.es_reference: Su énfasis es claro: velar, estar listos, permanecer fieles. Las parábolas refuerzan este mensaje: diez vírgenes—cinco preparadas, cinco insensatas; siervos a los que se les confían talentos—fieles o infieles; personas haciendo su vida diaria—repentinamente separadas. El problema no es cuándo. El problema es la preparación.

blocks.en: "But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father." — Matthew 24:36
blocks.es_reference: "Pero del día y la hora nadie sabe, ni aun los ángeles de los cielos, sino sólo mi Padre." — Mateo 24:36

blocks.en: Paul's Teaching: Comfort, Clarity, and the Day of the Lord
blocks.es_reference: La Enseñanza de Pablo: Consuelo, Claridad y el Día del Señor

blocks.en: The Apostle Paul gives both comfort and clarity regarding the end. In 1 Thessalonians 4:13‑18, he addresses the grief of believers who had lost loved ones before Christ's return. He assures them: "The Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God. And the dead in Christ will rise first. Then we who are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And thus we shall always be with the Lord."
blocks.es_reference: El apóstol Pablo da tanto consuelo como claridad con respecto al fin. En 1 Tesalonicenses 4:13-18, aborda el dolor de los creyentes que habían perdido seres queridos antes del regreso de Cristo. Les asegura: "Porque el Señor mismo con voz de mando, con voz de arcángel, y con trompeta de Dios, descenderá del cielo; y los muertos en Cristo resucitarán primero. Luego nosotros los que vivimos, los que hayamos quedado, seremos arrebatados juntamente con ellos en las nubes para recibir al Señor en el aire, y así estaremos siempre con el Señor".

blocks.en: This is not a theological curiosity; it is a word of comfort. The resurrection of the dead and the gathering of believers are certain. The Day of the Lord, however, comes like a thief in the night—unexpected, sudden, and decisive. For the unbeliever, it brings destruction; for the believer, it brings deliverance. Therefore, Paul urges, "Let us not sleep, as others do, but let us watch and be sober" (1 Thessalonians 5:6).
blocks.es_reference: Esta no es una curiosidad teológica; es una palabra de consuelo. La resurrección de los muertos y la reunión de los creyentes son ciertas. El Día del Señor, sin embargo, viene como ladrón en la noche—inesperado, repentino y decisivo. Para el incrédulo, trae destrucción; para el creyente, trae liberación. Por lo tanto, Pablo exhorta: "No durmamos como los demás, sino velemos y seamos sobrios" (1 Tesalonicenses 5:6).

blocks.en: "For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a shout... and the dead in Christ will rise first." — 1 Thessalonians 4:16
blocks.es_reference: "Porque el Señor mismo con voz de mando... descenderá del cielo; y los muertos en Cristo resucitarán primero." — 1 Tesalonicenses 4:16

blocks.en: The Millennial Views: A Responsible Diversity (Expanded)
blocks.es_reference: Las Visiones del Milenio: Una Diversidad Responsable

blocks.en: Faithful believers have differed on the nature of the millennium—the thousand‑year reign mentioned in Revelation 20. Three main views have emerged within evangelical theology. Each attempts to interpret the same biblical texts, but they arrive at different conclusions about the timing and nature of Christ's reign.
blocks.es_reference: Creyentes fieles han diferido sobre la naturaleza del milenio—el reinado de mil años mencionado en Apocalipsis 20. Tres visiones principales han surgido dentro de la teología evangélica. Cada una intenta interpretar los mismos textos bíblicos, pero llegan a conclusiones diferentes sobre el tiempo y la naturaleza del reinado de Cristo.

blocks.en: Premillennialism (especially Dispensational Premillennialism) – This view holds that Christ will return before a literal thousand‑year reign on earth. It became the dominant position in many evangelical circles in the 20th century, largely through the influence of the Scofield Reference Bible (1909) and later through popular authors like Hal Lindsey (The Late Great Planet Earth) and Tim LaHaye (Left Behind). Dispensational premillennialism teaches a sharp distinction between Israel and the church, a pre‑tribulation rapture of believers, and a future literal kingdom centered in Jerusalem. It is often associated with a very literal interpretation of Old Testament prophecies about Israel's restoration. While highly popular in many Bible churches and independent evangelical congregations, critics within premillennialism itself (such as historic premillennialists) reject the pre‑tribulation rapture and the rigid separation of Israel and the church.
blocks.es_reference: Premilenialismo (especialmente Premilenialismo Dispensacional) – Esta visión sostiene que Cristo regresará antes de un reinado literal de mil años en la tierra. Se convirtió en la posición dominante en muchos círculos evangélicos en el siglo XX, en gran parte a través de la influencia de la Biblia de Referencia Scofield (1909) y luego a través de autores populares como Hal Lindsey (La Agonía del Gran Planeta Tierra) y Tim LaHaye (Dejados Atrás). El premilenialismo dispensacional enseña una distinción aguda entre Israel y la iglesia, un arrebatamiento pretribulacional de los creyentes y un reino literal futuro centrado en Jerusalén. A menudo se asocia con una interpretación muy literal de las profecías del Antiguo Testamento sobre la restauración de Israel. Aunque muy popular en muchas iglesias bíblicas y congregaciones evangélicas independientes, los críticos dentro del premilenialismo mismo (como los premilenialistas históricos) rechazan el arrebatamiento pretribulacional y la rígida separación entre Israel y la iglesia.

blocks.en: Postmillennialism – This view teaches that Christ will return after a period of gospel‑inspired moral and spiritual progress, culminating in a millennial age of Christian influence. Postmillennialism flourished in the 19th century, an age of great optimism. Many believed that through education, missionary effort, and social reform, the world was steadily improving. The abolition of slavery, the expansion of democratic governments, and the spread of the Bible seemed to signal that the kingdom of God was advancing toward a golden age. At the end of that age, Christ would return. Two world wars and the horrors of the 20th century shattered that optimism for most, but postmillennialism still has advocates (often in Reformed and Presbyterian circles) who see the Great Commission slowly but surely bringing the nations to Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Postmilenialismo – Esta visión enseña que Cristo regresará después de un período de progreso moral y espiritual inspirado por el evangelio, culminando en una era milenial de influencia cristiana. El postmilenialismo floreció en el siglo XIX, una era de gran optimismo. Muchos creían que a través de la educación, el esfuerzo misionero y la reforma social, el mundo mejoraba constantemente. La abolición de la esclavitud, la expansión de los gobiernos democráticos y la difusión de la Biblia parecían señalar que el reino de Dios avanzaba hacia una era dorada. Al final de esa era, Cristo regresaría. Dos guerras mundiales y los horrores del siglo XX destrozaron ese optimismo para la mayoría, pero el postmilenialismo todavía tiene defensores (a menudo en círculos Reformados y Presbiterianos) que ven la Gran Comisión lenta pero seguramente trayendo las naciones a Cristo.

blocks.en: Amillennialism – This view interprets the millennium symbolically as the present reign of Christ from heaven through His church. It sees the binding of Satan (Revelation 20:1‑3) as having already occurred in Christ's earthly ministry and resurrection. The thousand years represent the entire church age between Christ's first and second coming. This view has been held by Augustine, Calvin, and most of the Reformers, and remains common in Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, and many Baptist traditions. William Barclay, whose commentary on Revelation is widely respected, held to an amillennial perspective. The strength of amillennialism is that it keeps the focus on Christ's present reign and the believer's spiritual victory, without requiring detailed speculation about a future earthly kingdom. It does not deny a future return of Christ or a final judgment, but it sees the millennium as a present reality.
blocks.es_reference: Amilenialismo – Esta visión interpreta el milenio simbólicamente como el reinado presente de Cristo desde el cielo a través de Su iglesia. Ve la atadura de Satanás (Apocalipsis 20:1-3) como ya ocurrida en el ministerio terrenal y la resurrección de Cristo. Los mil años representan toda la era de la iglesia entre la primera y segunda venida de Cristo. Esta visión ha sido sostenida por Agustín, Calvino y la mayoría de los Reformadores, y permanece común en las tradiciones Luterana, Reformada, Anglicana y muchas Bautistas. William Barclay, cuyo comentario sobre Apocalipsis es ampliamente respetado, sostuvo una perspectiva amilenial. La fortaleza del amilenialismo es que mantiene el enfoque en el reinado presente de Cristo y la victoria espiritual del creyente, sin requerir especulación detallada sobre un futuro reino terrenal. No niega un regreso futuro de Cristo ni un juicio final, pero ve el milenio como una realidad presente.

blocks.en: What the Millennial Views Hold in Common
blocks.es_reference: Lo que las Visiones Milenarias Tienen en Común

blocks.en: All three views agree on the essentials: Christ will return bodily, visibly, and gloriously; the dead will rise; and God will consummate His kingdom in a new heaven and new earth. The unity of the church does not depend on solving this disagreement, but on agreeing that Christ is Lord and that we must be ready for His return.
blocks.es_reference: Las tres visiones concuerdan en lo esencial: Cristo regresará corporal, visible y gloriosamente; los muertos resucitarán; y Dios consumará Su reino en un nuevo cielo y una nueva tierra. La unidad de la iglesia no depende de resolver este desacuerdo, sino de concordar en que Cristo es Señor y que debemos estar listos para Su regreso.

blocks.en: "Behold, He is coming with clouds, and every eye will see Him." — Revelation 1:7
blocks.es_reference: "He aquí que viene con las nubes, y todo ojo le verá." — Apocalipsis 1:7

blocks.en: The Historical Context of Revelation: Suffering and Sovereignty
blocks.es_reference: El Contexto Histórico del Apocalipsis: Sufrimiento y Soberanía

blocks.en: William Barclay explains that Roman citizens were required to declare "Caesar is Lord" once a year to prove loyalty. This was not merely political; it was religious. Christians refused. They declared instead, "Jesus Christ is Lord." Because of this, they were excluded from the economy, from legal protection, and often from life itself. They were burned, crucified, torn apart by wild animals. John wrote Revelation from the island of Patmos—a place of forced exile and hard labor. He was suffering. He wrote to people who were suffering.
blocks.es_reference: William Barclay explica que los ciudadanos romanos estaban obligados a declarar "César es Señor" una vez al año para probar su lealtad. Esto no era meramente político; era religioso. Los cristianos se negaban. Declaraban en cambio: "Jesucristo es Señor". Por esto, fueron excluidos de la economía, de la protección legal y a menudo de la vida misma. Fueron quemados, crucificados, despedazados por animales salvajes. Juan escribió Apocalipsis desde la isla de Patmos—un lugar de exilio forzado y trabajos pesados. Estaba sufriendo. Escribió a personas que estaban sufriendo.

blocks.en: Revelation was not written to satisfy curiosity about the distant future. It was written to sustain faithfulness in the present. Its visions of beasts, plagues, and cosmic upheaval are not a secret code for the clever; they are a pastoral message for the persecuted. They say: God is on His throne. The Lamb will conquer. Do not give up.
blocks.es_reference: Apocalipsis no fue escrito para satisfacer la curiosidad sobre el futuro distante. Fue escrito para sostener la fidelidad en el presente. Sus visiones de bestias, plagas y trastornos cósmicos no son un código secreto para los astutos; son un mensaje pastoral para los perseguidos. Dicen: Dios está en Su trono. El Cordero vencerá. No se rindan.

blocks.en: "I, John, your brother and companion in the suffering and kingdom and patient endurance that are ours in Jesus, was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus." — Revelation 1:9
blocks.es_reference: "Yo Juan, vuestro hermano, y copartícipe vuestro en la tribulación, en el reino y en la paciencia de Jesucristo, estaba en la isla llamada Patmos, por causa de la palabra de Dios y el testimonio de Jesucristo." — Apocalipsis 1:9

blocks.en: Key Themes: Already / Not Yet, Signs, and God's Faithfulness
blocks.es_reference: Temas Clave: Ya / Todavía No, Señales y la Fidelidad de Dios

blocks.en: The New Testament consistently presents the Kingdom as already and not yet. It is already present in the ministry of Jesus and the indwelling of the Spirit. It is not yet fully consummated; we await the visible reign of Christ. This tension prevents two errors: over‑realized eschatology (acting as if everything is perfect now) and under‑realized eschatology (doing nothing because the future is all that matters).
blocks.es_reference: El Nuevo Testamento presenta consistentemente el Reino como ya y todavía no. Ya está presente en el ministerio de Jesús y la morada del Espíritu. Todavía no está plenamente consumado; esperamos el reinado visible de Cristo. Esta tensión previene dos errores: escatología sobre-realizada (actuar como si todo fuera perfecto ahora) y escatología sub-realizada (no hacer nada porque el futuro es lo único que importa).

blocks.en: Signs—wars, earthquakes, famines, persecution—are not countdown markers. Jesus said, "These things must happen, but the end is not yet" (Matthew 24:6). They characterize the entire age between Christ's first and second coming. They remind us that the world is not as it should be, and they push us toward prayer and mission.
blocks.es_reference: Las señales—guerras, terremotos, hambres, persecución—no son marcadores de cuenta regresiva. Jesús dijo: "Es necesario que todo esto acontezca; pero aún no es el fin" (Mateo 24:6). Caracterizan toda la era entre la primera y segunda venida de Cristo. Nos recuerdan que el mundo no es como debería ser, y nos empujan hacia la oración y la misión.

blocks.en: God's faithfulness is the bedrock of eschatological hope. What He has promised, He will perform. The resurrection of Jesus is the guarantee that the dead will rise. The outpouring of the Spirit is the firstfruits of the coming harvest. Because God is faithful, we can trust His promises about the future.
blocks.es_reference: La fidelidad de Dios es el fundamento de la esperanza escatológica. Lo que Él ha prometido, lo cumplirá. La resurrección de Jesús es la garantía de que los muertos resucitarán. El derramamiento del Espíritu son las primicias de la cosecha venidera. Porque Dios es fiel, podemos confiar en Sus promesas sobre el futuro.

blocks.en: 💡 The Wedding Invitation: A young woman receives an invitation to a wedding. She does not know the exact hour the groom will arrive, but she knows the day. She does not spend her time drawing charts of his route. She prepares. She cleans her dress, packs her bag, and waits with eager expectation. She is ready for when he comes. Eschatology is not about solving puzzles; it is about being dressed and waiting.
blocks.es_reference: 💡 La Invitación de Boda: Una joven recibe una invitación a una boda. No sabe la hora exacta en que llegará el novio, pero sabe el día. No pasa su tiempo dibujando gráficos de su ruta. Se prepara. Limpia su vestido, empaca su bolso y espera con anhelante expectación. Está lista para cuando él venga. La escatología no se trata de resolver acertijos; se trata de estar vestido y esperando.

blocks.en: Application: Hope, Watchfulness, Unity
blocks.es_reference: Aplicación: Esperanza, Vigilancia, Unidad

blocks.en: Hope: Christ will return. This is not wishful thinking; it is a certainty anchored in the resurrection. Hope pulls the believer through suffering, knowing that the present groaning will be swallowed up by glory.
blocks.es_reference: Esperanza: Cristo regresará. Esto no es un pensamiento deseoso; es una certeza anclada en la resurrección. La esperanza lleva al creyente a través del sufrimiento, sabiendo que el gemido presente será absorbido por la gloria.

blocks.en: Watchfulness: Because we do not know the day, we must live each day as if it could be today. Watchfulness is not anxious staring at the sky; it is faithful stewardship of time, treasure, and talent.
blocks.es_reference: Vigilancia: Porque no sabemos el día, debemos vivir cada día como si pudiera ser hoy. La vigilancia no es mirar ansiosamente al cielo; es mayordomía fiel del tiempo, los tesoros y los talentos.

blocks.en: Unity: Differences about the millennium or the timing of the rapture must not divide the body of Christ. We agree on the essentials: Christ will return bodily, the dead will rise, and God will make all things new. On non‑essentials, we extend grace.
blocks.es_reference: Unidad: Las diferencias sobre el milenio o el momento del arrebatamiento no deben dividir el cuerpo de Cristo. Concordamos en lo esencial: Cristo regresará corporalmente, los muertos resucitarán y Dios hará todas las cosas nuevas. En lo no esencial, extendemos gracia.

blocks.en: "Therefore comfort one another with these words." — 1 Thessalonians 4:18
blocks.es_reference: "Por tanto, alentaos los unos a los otros con estas palabras." — 1 Tesalonicenses 4:18

blocks.en: The doctrine of last things does not end with a chart. It ends with a question: Are you ready? Not ready because you have solved a prophetic puzzle, but ready because you are in Christ. The wise virgins could not lend oil; each must have their own relationship with the Bridegroom. That is the final message of eschatology: Be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
blocks.es_reference: La doctrina de las últimas cosas no termina con un gráfico. Termina con una pregunta: ¿Estás listo? No listo porque hayas resuelto un acertijo profético, sino listo porque estás en Cristo. Las vírgenes prudentes no podían prestar aceite; cada una debe tener su propia relación con el Esposo. Ese es el mensaje final de la escatología: Estén listos, porque el Hijo del Hombre viene a la hora que no piensan.

sa.prompt: Define eschatology and explain why the lesson says its focus is preparation rather than prediction.
sa.model: Eschatology, the doctrine of last things, addresses the culmination of God's redemptive plan: the return of Christ, the final judgment, the resurrection of the dead, and the eternal state of the righteous and the unrighteous. It is often treated as speculation, with charts, timelines, and the desire to know when, but Scripture redirects that desire: Jesus did not teach His followers how to calculate the end but how to be ready when it comes. History is moving toward a conclusion God has established; the question is not whether you can explain the end but whether you are prepared for it.

sa.prompt: What three questions did the disciples ask in Matthew 24, and why is it not always clear which event a given verse describes?
sa.model: They asked when the Temple would be destroyed, when He would return, and what the sign of the end of the age would be. Jesus answered them together, weaving near and far prophecies into one discourse: the Temple was destroyed in AD 70, fulfilling His words, while His return and the end of the age remain future. Because the answers are woven together it is not always clear which event a verse describes, and that is intentional: Jesus is not giving a timeline, He is shaping a life.

sa.prompt: How do the parables of Matthew 24–25 reinforce Jesus' emphasis about the end?
sa.model: His emphasis is to watch, be ready, and stay faithful. The ten virgins, five prepared and five foolish; the servants entrusted with talents, faithful or unfaithful; and people going about daily life who are suddenly separated all make the same point: the issue is not when, the issue is readiness. Of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels nor the Son, but only the Father.

sa.prompt: Summarize Paul's teaching in 1 Thessalonians 4–5 about the return of Christ and the Day of the Lord, and its purpose.
sa.model: Paul addresses the grief of believers who had lost loved ones before Christ's return and assures them that the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a shout, the voice of an archangel, and the trumpet of God; the dead in Christ will rise first, then the living will be caught up with them to meet the Lord in the air and be with Him always. This is a word of comfort, not a curiosity: the resurrection and gathering of believers are certain. The Day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night, bringing destruction for the unbeliever and deliverance for the believer, so Paul urges us not to sleep but to watch and be sober.

sa.prompt: Describe dispensational premillennialism: what it teaches, how it became dominant, and what historic premillennialists reject in it.
sa.model: It holds that Christ returns before a literal thousand-year reign on earth. It became dominant in many evangelical circles in the twentieth century through the Scofield Reference Bible (1909) and later popular authors such as Hal Lindsey and Tim LaHaye. It teaches a sharp distinction between Israel and the church, a pre-tribulation rapture, and a future literal kingdom centered in Jerusalem, with a very literal reading of Old Testament prophecies about Israel's restoration. Historic premillennialists reject the pre-tribulation rapture and the rigid separation of Israel and the church.

sa.prompt: Explain postmillennialism and why it flourished in the nineteenth century but lost ground in the twentieth.
sa.model: Postmillennialism teaches that Christ returns after a period of gospel-inspired moral and spiritual progress culminating in a millennial age of Christian influence. It flourished in the nineteenth century, an age of optimism when the abolition of slavery, the expansion of democratic governments, and the spread of the Bible seemed to signal the kingdom advancing toward a golden age. Two world wars and the horrors of the twentieth century shattered that optimism for most, but it still has advocates, often in Reformed and Presbyterian circles, who see the Great Commission slowly bringing the nations to Christ.

sa.prompt: Explain amillennialism, who has held it, and what the lesson calls its strength.
sa.model: Amillennialism interprets the millennium symbolically as the present reign of Christ from heaven through His church; the binding of Satan already occurred in Christ's earthly ministry and resurrection, and the thousand years represent the whole church age between His first and second coming. Augustine, Calvin, and most of the Reformers held it, and it remains common in Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, and many Baptist traditions; William Barclay held it too. Its strength is that it keeps the focus on Christ's present reign and the believer's spiritual victory without detailed speculation about a future earthly kingdom, while still affirming Christ's return and the final judgment.

sa.prompt: According to William Barclay, what was the historical situation behind Revelation, and what was the book written to do?
sa.model: Roman citizens had to declare 'Caesar is Lord' once a year, a religious as well as political act; Christians refused and declared 'Jesus Christ is Lord', so they were excluded from the economy, from legal protection, and often from life itself. John wrote from Patmos, a place of exile and hard labor, a suffering man writing to suffering people. Revelation was not written to satisfy curiosity about the distant future but to sustain faithfulness in the present: its visions are not a secret code for the clever but a pastoral message for the persecuted. God is on His throne, the Lamb will conquer, do not give up.

sa.prompt: Explain the 'already / not yet' tension of the Kingdom and the two errors it prevents. How should signs such as wars and earthquakes be understood?
sa.model: The Kingdom is already present in the ministry of Jesus and the indwelling of the Spirit, and not yet fully consummated, since we await Christ's visible reign. Holding the tension prevents over-realized eschatology, acting as if everything is perfect now, and under-realized eschatology, doing nothing because only the future matters. Signs such as wars, earthquakes, famines, and persecution are not countdown markers; Jesus said these things must happen but the end is not yet. They characterize the whole age between His comings, remind us the world is not as it should be, and push us toward prayer and mission.

sa.prompt: What do all three millennial views hold in common, and how does the lesson apply eschatology to hope, watchfulness, and unity?
sa.model: All three agree that Christ will return bodily, visibly, and gloriously, that the dead will rise, and that God will consummate His kingdom in a new heaven and new earth; the unity of the church rests on that, not on solving the disagreement. Hope: Christ's return is a certainty anchored in the resurrection, pulling the believer through suffering. Watchfulness: since we do not know the day we live each day as if it could be today, not by staring at the sky but by faithful stewardship of time, treasure, and talent. Unity: differences about the millennium or the timing of the rapture must not divide the body; we agree on the essentials and extend grace on non-essentials. Eschatology ends with a question, Are you ready? Ready not because you solved a puzzle but because you are in Christ; the wise virgins could not lend their oil.
